title: Hai Rui Buys a Coffin Before Criticizing the Emperor
text:
By 1566 the Jiajing Emperor of the Ming dynasty had ruled China for more than forty years. For much of that time he had withdrawn from government, rarely holding court, absorbed in Daoist rituals meant to bring him immortality, while officials governed in his name and corruption spread.

Hai Rui was a minor official in the Ministry of Revenue, known for strict honesty. He wrote a memorial to the emperor criticizing him directly: for neglecting the state, for his superstitions, for his treatment of his family and ministers, and for the suffering of the people. He wrote that the realm had long thought the emperor in the wrong.

According to the official History of Ming, before submitting it he bought a coffin, said farewell to his wife and children, and waited for punishment, expecting to be executed.

The emperor read the memorial, threw it to the ground and ordered Hai Rui arrested before he could escape. A eunuch told him that Hai Rui was known for his foolish stubbornness, had already bought his coffin, that his servants had fled, and that he would not run. The emperor picked up the memorial and read it again and again. Hai Rui was imprisoned, but the emperor died months later, and Hai Rui was released and restored to office.
lesson: Honest criticism of those above you may cost a great deal. Decide in advance what you are willing to pay, and then say what is true.
source: Ming Shi (History of Ming), Biography of Hai Rui; Hai Rui, Memorial on Public Order (Zhi An Shu)
